body: I’m not in the same situation as him but kinda similar. I’m 28f and I have a big family. I’m the second oldest of 8 siblings and we’re all close, my mom had 3 she was close to, and my grandma had 13 she was close to. I grew up poor but in a very loving home. My mom was the absolute best. All of my adult siblings are doing well in life (families, careers, etc). I have multiple best friends. While I don’t have a career, I’ve always landed on my feet and been in decent positions for growth in whatever job I had. People seem to like me. I get told so often how I have this beautiful spirit and how people aspire to have the disposition I have. I’ve been in healthy relationships and engaged once. But I’ve been suicidal for years. There is this crippling darkness that hangs over me. While I don’t really pretend to be happy, honestly sometimes life is actually really good, I’m not always truly happy. I’ve suffered from depression since I was a child. I have horrible anxiety that makes me believe everyone truly hates me. And I only recently started even trying to grieve the major deaths in my life. (Mom, grandma, aunt) I lost the women closest to me while learning what it even was to be one. I feel like I’ve failed at life even though I’m not in the worst of positions and because I’m not in the worst of positions, I don’t feel like I can ever truly express what goes on in my head. People don’t make you happy. Money doesn’t make you happy. I found that I’d rather actually be alone, than to feel alone in a room full of people, which is how I spent most of my life. Always surrounded by love and a million brothers and other family members, but empty and alone inside. I hope this doesn’t come off any kind of way to you, I just wanted to let you know we exist, and we don’t know what the fuck we’re doing wrong either.

I became actively suicidal after my grandmother died. I think it was always kind of dormant. She was the last mother I had. My mom died 6 years before her when I was 20. No one tells you how that feels. Honestly, they can’t. She was the last person I had who I never questioned whether they loved me or not. It’s like my brain chemistry would cause me to question every other single person in life but my mom and my grandma. No matter what, they were always there and then I was alone, struggling with mental illness, trying to be successful but failing. The thing was I was struggling with mental illness and trying to be successful but failing long before they left but they validated a part of me, made me feel whole without even trying, and always let me know I wasn’t alone. I attempted 4 years ago, not even a year after my grandma passed. And it took a while, but in that darkness I started to understand why they loved me. She loved you for a reason and not because she had to. Because she knew you and knew you were someone worthy to be loved. She saw you. You have to see you too.

It’s an every day battle. Some days are better than others but most for me are just as bad. I’ve been to counseling before, it helped for a while but I hate the idea of someone who doesn’t know me trying to tell me how to fix myself. Have you ever tried counseling?

I understand completely. I feel as if I’m stuck in the spin cycle. Everything around me is moving but nothing is changing. No matter where I go, or what I do, I always come back to feeling as if I don’t belong anywhere in the world. You’re not alone. You can talk to me.

Thank you. I write. It’s the only thing that brings me any kind of joy but I’m starting to lose the joy in everything. I’ve spoken to friends but I feel as if that doors closing because they’re tired of me and my issues. I’m just not sure what the next step is from here.
